newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM Cargo operating revs up 5 pct in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: KLM Cargo operating revs up 5 pct in 96/97.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM said on Wednesday its cargo arm boosted operating revenues by five percent to 1.74 billion guilders in the fiscal year ended March 31. Capacity and traffic at KLM Cargo both increased by two percent year-on-year.
Traffic in revenue tonne kilometres (RTKs) stood at 3.88 billion RTK for the year and capacity in available tonne kilometres(ATKs) at 5.85 billion ATK.
However, the cargo load factor decreased fractionally from 66.7 to 66.3 percent.
Yields rose by three percent to 44.9 guilder cents per RTK.
Unit revenues also increased by the same amount to 29.8 Dutch cents per ATK.
"The policy of restricting capacity in a situation of limited market growth had a positive effect, but primarily in the second half of the year," KLM said in a statement.

Capacity grew seven percent during the summer of 1996, outstripping traffic growth. But capacity was reduced to five percent year-on-year growth in the winter. Traffic decreased by two percent during this period.
For the three months ended March 31, KLM Cargo saw an 11 percent increase in operating revenue to 445 million guilders.
Traffic and capacity fell for the fourth quarter. Cargo traffic fell by three percent to 911 million RTK and capacity fell by five percent to 1.36 billion ATK.

However, cargo yields increased by 14 percent to 48.8 guilder cents per RTK and unit revenues also rose, by 17 percent to 32.6 guilder cents per ATK. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom +44-171-542-7706 Fax+5017
